# Hostile-but-tolerant input fixture

A full 6-file input set derived from `trust_domain/synthetic/sample`
(generated by `trust_domain/synthetic/generator.py`), then deliberately
mutated with real-world CSV quirks that a genuine PMS export is likely to
contain and that the loader must tolerate rather than crash on:

- **Mixed date formats.** Some rows use ISO (`YYYY-MM-DD`), others use
  NZ-common `DD/MM/YYYY` — including `invoice_register.csv`'s `INV-00237`
  (the ERR-10 / R10 seeded violation), specifically to prove that a
  date-format switch on just one side of a cross-record comparison doesn't
  silently break the comparison (see `test_hostile_ingestion.py`).
- **Blank rows.** Each of `matter_register.csv`, `client_ledger.csv`,
  `trust_bank_statement.csv`, and `allocations.csv` has one row where every
  field is empty (trailing commas only) — the kind of row Excel leaves
  behind after a deleted line.
- **Extra, unexpected columns.** Every file has one additional column not
  in the engine's internal schema (`internal_note`, `source_system_id`,
  `pms_sync_flag`, `gst_incl`, `reviewer_initials`, `notes` on
  `allocations.csv`) — the kind of column a firm's own export tool adds
  that the engine has no reason to know about.
- **Windows line endings.** Every CSV in this fixture is CRLF-terminated, as
  a real export from a Windows practice-management system would be. The
  repository's `.gitattributes` exempts this folder from line-ending
  normalisation so the trait survives checkout on every OS.
- **Numeric formatting noise.** A few amount fields use a thousands
  separator and/or surrounding whitespace (`" 8,500.00 "`, `"125,000.00"`,
  `"2,500.00"`).

This fixture is expected to load and run through the full pipeline
successfully, producing 18 seeded violations, measured as at the injected
`generated_at` date (2026-06-25) — see
`test_hostile_ingestion.py::test_hostile_tolerant_fixture_runs_clean`.
(The fixture was frozen from the clean synthetic sample before the Phase 3
real-decision scenarios were added, so it carries fewer seeds than the
current clean sample. It was originally asserted as 19 while the ageing
rules used the wall clock; B048, dated 2026-06-24, is correctly below R04's
5-day threshold at the fixed reference date.)

Separate, narrower fixtures for inputs that *should* raise a clear
`ConfigError` (unparseable date, non-numeric value, missing column, blank
identifier, empty file) are built inline in `test_hostile_ingestion.py`
using `tmp_path`, matching the existing convention in `test_ingestion.py`,
rather than checked in here — each is a one-line mutation and doesn't
need a static fixture file.
